name: BLS Local Area Unemployment Statistics (LAUS)
what_it_measures: Monthly unemployment rate and labor force estimates for ~7,000 areas including every US county.
coverage: national (all US counties and other LAUS areas)
granularity: county (also state, metro division, and some sub-county areas)
history_available: decades (LAUS series generally run back to the 1990s or earlier for most counties)
access_method: Free BLS API v2 (registration gives a free key with a higher daily query cap; unregistered use is allowed at a lower cap) returning JSON by series ID, or a bulk flat-file download at download.bls.gov/pub/time.series/la/ with no key at all.
license: US government work; BLS data is public domain / free to use, no login required for the bulk flat files.
rate_limit: Not independently confirmed for the current API in this run; third-party sources describe a daily query cap that is higher with a free registered key. The no-key bulk flat-file route has no such limit.
fills_gap: None of the current neighborhood-growth sources (housing_database, rezonings in app/sources/development.py; subway_access, planned_catalysts in app/sources/transit.py; nypd_felonies, liquor_licenses, future_floodplain in app/sources/livability.py) generalize outside NYC — most are NYC Open Data / Socrata feeds (planned_catalysts instead reads a local catalysts.yaml config, not Socrata). census_acs.py is national-grade ACS data in principle but is hardcoded to NYC's 5 counties and has no employment-status variable (no B23025-type field) in its VARS dict. County-level LAUS unemployment is a standard, nationally-available economic-health signal that would give the growth score a real input anywhere in the US.
caveats: NYC's 5 boroughs are each their own county (New York, Kings, Queens, Bronx, Richmond), so county-level LAUS does give borough-level differentiation inside NYC today — it's not zero signal, just coarser than NTA. Full within-borough differentiation would need the CBSA/area-model migration mentioned in backend/CLAUDE.md for non-NYC metros, and a finer-than-county series (none found) for NYC itself.
Monthly cadence is overkill for a slow-moving structural indicator; a quarterly refresh would be plenty and cheaper on the request budget.
Confirm the current (not historical) BLS API v2 endpoint and rate-limit numbers directly at bls.gov before implementing — this run relied on secondary sources for limit specifics.
recommendation_note: Free, genuinely national, long history — a solid growth-score input. Recommended; inside NYC it gives only borough-level (not NTA-level) differentiation, but it generalizes immediately to every other US county, which is the project's stated goal.
